🇲🇽🇨🇳 <u>SINALOA SELLS CHINA UP TO 1.2 MILLION TONS OF SORGHUM</u>

While Washington threatens tariffs, Mexico keeps opening markets. Sinaloa just signed a letter of intent with China's Sichuan Yourong Group for up to 1.2 million tons of red sorghum, with the first five containers leaving the port of Topolobampo for quality tests — the grain is headed for baijiu, China's national liquor. The buyers tested it against Australian sorghum and came back sold: "Today we can say we believe we have found the best sorghum in the world." Diversification is not a speech. It is cargo leaving Topolobampo.
banner: SORGHUM: CHINA BUYS 1.2M TONS FROM SINALOA

🇲🇽📊 <u>MEXICO'S POVERTY LINE HITS 4,884 PESOS AS FOOD COSTS OUTRUN INFLATION</u>

Per El Economista's weekly data wrap: INEGI's July poverty lines put the basic basket of food and services at 4,884.09 pesos per person in urban Mexico, up 3.5% annually — running above the 3.1% headline inflation. The food-only threshold rose 3.8% in the cities to 2,545.72 pesos, driven by meals away from home (+6.0%) and potatoes, up 62.3% in a year.

The official yardstick for what it costs not to be poor keeps rising faster than the CPI.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S PHONE REGISTRY TOPS 71 MILLION LINES AS FIRST CUTOFF TAKES EFFECT</u>

Mexico's CRT confirmed there would be no extension: unregistered mobile lines ending in 0 began losing service this weekend, with the shutdown rolling out gradually over 72 hours. Suspended numbers are not lost — service restores automatically once the owner completes registration, at no cost and with no balance required.

71 million lines are already verified in the national registry, built to choke off extortion calls.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>79% OF MEXICANS BACK SANCTIONS ON MEDIA THAT DECEIVE AUDIENCES</u>

Mexico's corporate media spent two weeks crying censorship over the audience-rights guidelines. A new De Las Heras poll: 79% of Mexicans believe the government should sanction outlets that deceive audiences with false information, and 78% want a clear line between news and paid content. Only 28% buy the censorship narrative.

Sheinbaum stressed her guidelines propose neither sanctions nor content control — just ethics codes and ombudsmen to handle audience complaints: "Como decía el presidente López Obrador: tonto es el que cree que el pueblo es tonto."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>GRUPO MÉXICO STALLS ON FINAL 500M PESOS OF RÍO SONORA CLEANUP DEBT</u>

Germán Larrea's Grupo México is dragging its feet on the last 500 million pesos of the 1.5 billion it pledged for Río Sonora remediation — a third of the deal signed with the federal government in December 2025, twelve years after the worst toxic spill in the history of Mexican mining. Contralínea reports the government's ultimatum expires August 21; if the company doesn't pay, the criminal complaint Semarnat filed with the FGR in 2023 — frozen under the payment deal — reactivates.

The money is earmarked for water treatment plants for the affected towns. And while Larrea stalls, his Ferromex subsidiary spilled another 70,300 liters of sodium hydrosulfide in Naco, Sonora, on July 26.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US COURT GREENLIGHTS BORDER WALL ON TOHONO O'ODHAM LAND BETWEEN SONORA AND ARIZONA</u>

A federal court in Washington rejected the Tohono O'odham Nation's request for a preliminary injunction against border wall construction on its reservation straddling Sonora and Arizona. The O'odham — one of Sonora's eight indigenous peoples, split by a border drawn through their ancestral territory — warn the wall will hit sacred sites including the Quitobaquito springs and the Las Playas intaglios, and communities with historic ties on both sides. The lawsuit continues; the injunction denial means construction doesn't have to wait.

"We know a border wall will destroy our sacred sites, damage our environment and further divide the O'odham people," said tribal chairman Verlon José.
banner: WALL OK'D ON O'ODHAM SACRED LAND

🇲🇽🌎 <u>LANDAU PREACHES 'MUTUAL RESPECT' HOURS AFTER MOCKING MEXICO VISA BAN</u>

US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau wants Mexico to move on: the monarch butterflies' arrival is "a good reminder of the enduring and symbiotic relationship between the US and Mexico," and neither country should let "the occasional outbreak of political drama" distract from security, migration and trade cooperation.

The "drama," posted by Landau himself just hours earlier, was a taunt over Washington's revocation of Andrés López Beltrán's visa: "¿Estás disfrutando el espectáculo? Rellena tus palomitas — te encantará lo que sigue."
